newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut bourse gets new bank index.
newsitem.headline: Beirut bourse gets new bank index.

text.p: Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest introduced a new banking sector index on Tuesday for the Beirut Stock Exchange.

Only Banque Audi and Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce are currently traded on the market but two more banks are seeking listings and Lebanon Invest said the banking sector was becoming increasingly important to the market.
"We think the sector is going to be very important," said Alain Balian, a deputy manager at Lebanon Invest. "Within a couple of months it will be a very important index."
Lebanon Invest already issues a daily Share Price Index (LISPI) for the Beirut Stock Exchange.

"Keeping in mind the importance of the banking sector to the Lebanese economy and as more banks are anticipated for listing on the exchange in the near future, LIBX...will be an important measure of bank share performance," Balian said.
LIBX followed the same concept as LISPI, introduced in April 1996, and was calculated through a geometric mean of bank share prices, he added.
It takes its base as 100 on January 20, 1997, the day Banque Audi became the second bank traded on the Bourse.
